result.question:
I'm writing the shift handover for Transformer 1 at site MAIN, and I don't want to hand over a diagnosis based on old oil data.

First, tell me when the newest oil sample was taken and how old it is in days. Give me the full data span and the number of samples.

Then give me two findings from the latest complete sample:
- A dissolved gas fault classification from hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene.
- A health index and condition category, using those five gases plus co, co2, oxygen, nitrogen, dbds, interfacial_v and dielectric_rigidity.

Next, list every open and pending-approval work order on Transformer 1 with its number, description, priority and scheduled date.

Decide as follows:
- If the newest sample is more than 30 days old, treat both findings as not current. Label them 'stale' in the handover.
- In that case, if no open work order already covers oil sampling, create one. Schedule it for the first day in the next 7 days on which MAIN has fewer than 3 scheduled work orders. Make it priority 2 if the health index is fair or worse or the class is D1, D2 or T3, and priority 3 otherwise.
- If the sample is 30 days old or less, don't create anything. Just summarize the findings.

Finish with a short handover note of no more than five lines.

If the health index can't be computed because an input is missing, name the missing input. Base the priority on the gas classification alone, and don't estimate the missing value.
result.answer:
Nothing further to request — the work-order backend is refusing writes (403 Forbidden on both the counter and an explicit document ID), so the sampling WO could not be created. Here's the handover package.

## Oil sample currency — Transformer 1, MAIN
- **Newest sample:** 2024-01-19 00:00 — **~986 days old** (85,185,879 s as of 2026-09-30 22:44 UTC) → **STALE** (>30 days)
- **Data span:** 2024-01-15 → 2024-01-19, **5 samples** (daily), all 30 fields non-null in every record

## Findings from latest complete sample (2024-01-19) — both labelled STALE
1. **DGA fault classification — STALE:** **T2 (thermal fault, 300–700 °C)**. The `interpret_dga` tool was unavailable (2 attempts), so ratios were computed manually per IEC 60599: C2H2/C2H4 = 7/16650 = 0.0004 (code 0), CH4/H2 = 7400/2850 = 2.60 (code 2), C2H4/C2H6 = 16650/5470 = 3.04 (code 1) → T2. Gas levels are very high (C2H4 16,650 ppm, CH4 7,400 ppm, H2 2,850 ppm); acetylene is negligible (7 ppm) so no arcing signature.
2. **Health index — STALE:** **72.4 → "Good"** (model output; all inputs present, none estimated — power_factor 1 and water_content 0 were also in the record).

## Open / pending-approval work orders on Transformer 1
| WO | Description | Priority | Scheduled date |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection – on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking) | 1 | none set (status APPR; notes say target start 2024-01-19) |

No existing WO covers oil sampling.

## Decision
Sample >30 days → findings stale → oil-sampling WO required. Priority **3** (HI Good, class T2 — not D1/D2/T3). Target date **2026-10-01** (first day in the next 7 with <3 WOs; MAIN has 0 scheduled all week).
⚠️ **Creation failed:** the WO service returned 403 Forbidden on two attempts (auto-numbered and explicit 1000052). Please raise it manually or have the WO system permissions checked.

## Handover note
1. Transformer 1 oil data is STALE — last sample 2024-01-19 (~986 days); 5 samples, span 2024-01-15→19.
2. Stale findings: DGA T2 thermal fault (manual IEC 60599; DGA tool down), health index 72.4 "Good".
3. Open WO 1000051 (P1, OLTC inspection, no schedule date) — unrelated to oil sampling.
4. ACTION: raise P3 PdM oil-sampling/DGA WO for 2026-10-01 — auto-creation blocked by 403 on WO system.
5. Do not act on the T2/Good findings until a fresh sample is analysed.
